data.title: Fitch Confirms Alliança RD Rating and Withdraws Coverage Amid Reorganization
data.description:
Allianca Saude e Participacoes SA – ALLIAR ( (BR:AALR3) ) has provided an announcement.

Fitch Ratings has maintained Alliança Saúde e Participações S.A.’s long-term national rating at RD(bra), reflecting the company’s ongoing extrajudicial reorganization process now under judicial review in São Paulo. At the same time, Fitch has withdrawn its rating coverage of Alliança for commercial reasons, and the company has pledged to keep investors informed of any material developments in line with CVM corporate governance rules.

The reaffirmation of the RD(bra) rating underscores Alliança’s distressed credit profile during its reorganization, while the withdrawal of coverage removes a key external benchmark for investors tracking its recovery prospects. The company’s commitment to timely disclosure aims to mitigate information gaps for shareholders and the market as the court evaluates the restructuring plan and its implications for creditors and other stakeholders.

data.title: Liberty Puerto Rico considers standalone structure amid debt talks
data.description:
An update from Liberty Global LiLAC ( (LILA) ) is now available.

Liberty Latin America disclosed that negotiations with certain secured lenders of its Puerto Rico unit over a potential restructuring of term loans, senior secured notes due 2027 and 2029, and related UnSub facilities have taken place but are no longer ongoing. On September 11, 2026, a creditor steering committee counterproposal outlined a structure that would reconsolidate existing entities, refinance $410 million of UnSub debt with new first‑out financing, and potentially separate Liberty Puerto Rico into a standalone “New LPR.”

The latest term sheets detail a mix of new money first‑out notes or term loans, extended revolving credit facility terms, and second‑out takeback debt capped around 4.0x leverage, alongside significant equity reallocation to participating first‑lien creditors. Liberty Latin America’s retained stake would be largely reduced or reshaped through minority equity and warrant rights, signalling a possible shift in control of the Puerto Rico operations and material implications for recoveries across the company’s secured creditor base, although no binding agreement has yet been reached.
